seeds.ti: WEM is a set of products, and WFM is one of them
seeds.ex: WEM is a set of products, and WFM is one of them. Recording, screen recording, quality, performance, speech and text analytics, and workforce management are the WEM list. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.

seeds.ti: SIP, RTP, and what the trunk is doing
seeds.ex: SIP, RTP, and what the trunk is doing. SIP sets the call up. RTP moves the audio. They are different protocols, and Genesys trunks speak both. Last checked 2026-10.
seeds.eg: RFC 3261 is the Session Initiation Protocol. An INVITE offers a session, responses such as 100, 180, and 200 move the dialog along, and ACK confirms the 200.

seeds.ti: Predictive routing is a KPI model with a timeout
seeds.ex: Predictive routing is a KPI model with a timeout. Predictive routing can run for everyone, in a comparison test, or at a fixed 80/20 split you cannot edit. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
seeds.eg: The queue article describes three modes. Comparison test mode measures predictive routing against a baseline. Use for all interactions sends everything through the model.

seeds.ti: Predictive Engagement watches the site, not the queue math
seeds.ex: Predictive Engagement watches the site, not the queue math. It predicts what a visitor is trying to do and offers a message, a chat, content, or a flow. Predictive routing is a different feature on the queue. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
seeds.eg: The About Predictive Engagement page calls it a Genesys Cloud AI feature that analyzes how visitors behave on websites, predicts the outcomes they are trying to reach, and personal

seeds.ti: Genesys Cloud Voice is the other door
seeds.ex: Genesys Cloud Voice is the other door. If Genesys is the carrier, you buy numbers in a region that offers voice, and emergency is part of that product story rather than your trunk. Last checked 2026-10.
seeds.eg: The Voice regions article lists where Genesys Cloud Voice operates and where it does not. Country tables restrict DID, toll-free, domestic, and international calling.

seeds.ti: Direct routing still uses a queue
seeds.ex: Direct routing still uses a queue. The customer reaches a dedicated person. Wrap-up still exists, because the interaction is ACD. Last checked 2026-10.
seeds.eg: The direct routing overview says you route voice, SMS, and email to dedicated personnel, and the customer does not wait for the next available agent.

docs.ti: Five routing methods
docs.ex: Five routing methods. Standard, predictive, bullseye, preferred agent, and conditional group routing are the methods on a queue. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The routing settings article lists those five. Standard is the default. It offers the interaction to the next agent according to the evaluation method you picked.

docs.ti: All skills, best available, or disregard
docs.ex: All skills, best available, or disregard. The evaluation method is how standard and bullseye decide that an agent “has the skills.” Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: All skills matching selects the longest-idle agent who has every required skill. Proficiency is not the sort.

docs.ti: Conversation score and priority score
docs.ex: Conversation score and priority score. One priority point on conversation score is worth 60,000 milliseconds of arrival time. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: Conversation score combines arrival time and priority. The evaluation article says one priority point equals 60,000 milliseconds, so a higher priority jumps the line as if it had a

docs.ti: Preferred agents are tried first

docs.ti: Conditional group routing borrows agents carefully
docs.ex: Conditional group routing borrows agents carefully. A rule is a KPI plus agent availability. The other queue must be able to spare the people. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The overview describes conditional group routing as sharing groups of agents between queues based on rules.

docs.ti: Utilization and Not Responding
docs.ex: Utilization and Not Responding. A fully utilized agent is skipped. An agent who ignores an alert becomes Not Responding. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: Defaults from the utilization article: one voice call, one email, one callback, up to four chats, up to four messages, and up to four workitems.

docs.ti: Two Architect bot types, plus Copilot beside the agent
docs.ex: Two Architect bot types, plus Copilot beside the agent. A bot flow talks to the customer. Agent Copilot talks to the agent. They are different products on different pages. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: Architect documents Genesys Dialog Engine Bot Flows and Genesys Digital Bot Flows as flow types. An inbound flow calls them with the matching action.

docs.ti: Dialog Engine bot flows are voice and digital intents
docs.ex: Dialog Engine bot flows are voice and digital intents. You build the bot in Architect, then the inbound flow calls it. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The Dialog Engine article and the inbound-bot article show a bot that asks a question and returns an intent the flow can branch on.

docs.ti: Digital bot flows are a different call
docs.ex: Digital bot flows are a different call. Message experiences use Digital Bot Flows and Call Digital Bot Flow. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The digital bot article describes Genesys Digital Bot Flows for message experiences. They are Architect flows, and they are not the Dialog Engine type with a renamed action.

docs.ti: Every bot has a failure output to a queue
docs.ex: Every bot has a failure output to a queue. No-match, timeout, and error are normal. The queue is the design. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The inbound bot article’s useful pattern is a question, an intent, and a way out. Treat failure as a path you draw, not as an exception.

docs.ti: Agent Copilot assists the person who stayed on the interaction
docs.ex: Agent Copilot assists the person who stayed on the interaction. Knowledge, transcripts, scripts, next best action, and notes. The benefit is described as surviving a blind transfer. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The Agent Copilot overview lists knowledge articles, transcripts, custom scripts, next best action, and forms and notes: reason, resolution, and a possible wrap-up.

docs.ti: Tokens are a published allotment, and a FAQ ratio you re-read
docs.ex: Tokens are a published allotment, and a FAQ ratio you re-read. The overview publishes CX 4 token counts. The STA FAQ publishes how AI scoring spends them. Unconfirmed: Token ratios and allotments change. The numbers in this lesson match the pages as read for this lab on 14 October 2026. Re-open them. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The package overview lists 30 AI tokens for a named CX 4 user and 39 for a concurrent user. That sentence is the allotment story.

docs.ti: The AI exams are named on the catalog, one exam each
docs.ex: The AI exams are named on the catalog, one exam each. Two AI certifications. No invented exam codes. Unconfirmed: Course numbers were taken from the Genesys Cloud exams catalog as read on 14 October 2026. Confirm before you enroll. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: The Genesys Cloud exams page lists AI certifications separately from the Professional and Developer certifications and from the specialist exams.

docs.ti: The Developer Center is the map. This lab is not a client.
docs.ex: The Developer Center is the map. This lab is not a client.. Read the public docs. Do not point a tutorial at a production org. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: The Genesys Cloud Developer Center is the front door for the Platform API. The API explorer in this lab shows sample JSON shaped from the client-credentials guide and from admin li

docs.ti: Pick the grant that matches who the call runs as
docs.ex: Pick the grant that matches who the call runs as. Client credentials, authorization code with PKCE, and SAML2 Bearer are the grants to learn. Implicit is the one leaving. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: The create-an-OAuth-client article lists the grant types you can assign. Client credentials are for a service.

docs.ti: Client credentials have no user, so users/me is the wrong call
docs.ex: Client credentials have no user, so users/me is the wrong call. The token is the client. The guide shows that limit on purpose. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: The client-credentials guide shows a POST to the login host’s /oauth/token with HTTP Basic of the client id and secret, and grant_type=client_credentials.

docs.ti: Implicit grant is a migration, not a new design
docs.ex: Implicit grant is a migration, not a new design. The OAuth article dates the deprecation: after 25 May 2026. Unconfirmed: Confirm the deprecation sentence on the OAuth article before you enforce 25 May 2026 in a program plan. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: Token Implicit Grant returns a token in the browser redirect. That pattern is what the create-an-OAuth-client article marks deprecated after 25 May 2026.

docs.ti: Login host and API host are a pair you look up
docs.ex: Login host and API host are a pair you look up. US East is the pair this lab will quote in full. Other rows stay on the regions article. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: US East (N. Virginia, us-east-1) uses login.mypurecloud.com and, in the client-credentials guide, api.mypurecloud.com. US West (Oregon, us-west-2) uses login.usw2.pure.cloud.

docs.ti: Role and division pairs are the real permission
docs.ex: Role and division pairs are the real permission. A token opens the door the role allows, in the division the pair names. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: Divisions overview: objects live in one division, Home cannot be deleted, and the All division is the org-wide grant. OAuth clients do not escape that model.

docs.ti: SCIM and other directory sync still start with an OAuth client
docs.ex: SCIM and other directory sync still start with an OAuth client. The OAuth article points SCIM at a client. The client still has roles and a grant. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: Create an OAuth client is the article that tells you SCIM uses an OAuth client. Treat that client like any other service: a deliberate grant, least roles, a division pair, a secret

docs.ti: The flow types on the Architect home page
docs.ex: The flow types on the Architect home page. Architect is a list of flow types. Picking the wrong tab is the first defect. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The home page documents inbound call, inbound message, inbound email, inbound chat, outbound call, bot flow, common module, in-queue call, in-queue email, in-queue message, secure

docs.ti: Tasks, menus, and a way out
docs.ex: Tasks, menus, and a way out. An inbound call flow plays audio, collects input, and must transfer, hand off, or disconnect. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: About Architect describes linking actions: play audio, route to agents, queues, voicemail, numbers, or other flows, collect digits outside a menu, dip data, and branch with express

docs.ti: In-queue flows are the hold experience
docs.ex: In-queue flows are the hold experience. The caller is already queued. The in-queue flow is what they hear or read while ACD looks for an agent. Unconfirmed: The in-queue article also describes overall and recurring periods for email and message flows. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: For calls, Architect supplies a default in-queue flow built around a music action. Menus and reusable tasks are not available in that flow type.

docs.ti: Data actions and participant data
docs.ex: Data actions and participant data. A data action calls a system outside the flow. Participant data carries a value to the agent. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.

docs.ti: Common modules are how you stop copying tasks
docs.ex: Common modules are how you stop copying tasks. A common module is a flow type you call from other flows. The name is still unique inside that type. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: The Architect home page lists common module as its own type so you can build logic once and reuse it across flow types.

docs.ti: Secure call flows keep digits away from the recording
docs.ex: Secure call flows keep digits away from the recording. A secure flow is how a caller enters a card number without that audio being recorded or shown to the agent. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The Architect home page describes secure call flows as the way to stop system recording and agent access while a caller enters sensitive digits, such as a payment.

docs.ti: Call a bot from the inbound flow
docs.ex: Call a bot from the inbound flow. Dialog Engine bot flows and digital bot flows are Architect flow types. The inbound flow calls them. It does not become them. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: Genesys documents Dialog Engine Bot Flows for voice and digital flows, and Digital Bot Flows for message experiences.

docs.ti: Publish, division, and Flow Insights
docs.ex: Publish, division, and Flow Insights. A saved flow is a draft. The runtime uses the published version. Insights tell you whether anyone hit it. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: Create, edit, and publish are different moments. In-queue flows make that obvious because the default exists and still does nothing until publish.

docs.ti: Local site routing stays home until it cannot
docs.ex: Local site routing stays home until it cannot. Genesys uses Edges in the same site when it can. Another site is the exception. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The Edge group article says local site routing prefers same-site Edges to save bandwidth and latency.

docs.ti: Phone trunks, WebRTC, and inherit
docs.ex: Phone trunks, WebRTC, and inherit. WebRTC and SIP phones are phone trunks on the Edge group. Inherit is the default you should verify. Last checked 2026-10.

docs.ti: When the local Edge is offline
docs.ex: When the local Edge is offline. The documented failover is another site, if that site actually has the resource. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: Offline, at capacity, or missing the resource: those are the only reasons the article gives for leaving the site.

docs.ti: Choose Cloud, Premises, or both
docs.ex: Choose Cloud, Premises, or both. Use premises when the phones and the carrier are on your network. Use cloud when they are not. Use both only where each number has an owner. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: BYOC Cloud wants a public carrier and accepts internet RTP. BYOC Premises wants Edges close to phones and trunks.

docs.ti: A browser phone is still a network endpoint
docs.ex: A browser phone is still a network endpoint. WebRTC removes the desk set. It does not remove media engineering. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The Edge group article treats WebRTC as a phone trunk. The BYOC Cloud overview treats internet RTP as something you must judge.

docs.ti: Premises turn-up checklist
docs.ex: Premises turn-up checklist. Group, inherit, site, trunk, failover test, emergency owner. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: Create the Edge group on a low-latency network. Add the phone trunk. Confirm inherit on every Edge. Put the carrier trunk where the calls are.

docs.ti: Name the emergency owner before the DID
docs.ex: Name the emergency owner before the DID. Genesys is not responsible for emergency calls that ride a BYOC trunk. That sentence belongs in the design, not in the postmortem. Last checked 2026-10.

docs.ti: Emergency is a classification and a route
docs.ex: Emergency is a classification and a route. The default Emergency plan matches 911 and 933 in the US and Canada, and 142 in Switzerland. It still needs a route. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The number-plan article lists those defaults and the Suicide Prevention classification for 988 to +18002738255. Matching is not routing.

docs.ti: The location is a physical place
docs.ex: The location is a physical place. The quick start adds a location because services, including emergency, need a real site. Last checked 2026-10.

docs.ex: Voice coverage is a table, not a promise. Country rows decide DID, toll-free, domestic, and international. FedRAMP and the sovereign region add harder edges. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: The restrictions article is a matrix of countries and call types, plus two special sections.

docs.ti: Normalize toward E.164 on purpose
docs.ex: Normalize toward E.164 on purpose. Intra-country and inter-country plans normalize. Digit-length extensions and E.164 lists do not. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The number-plan article is specific. Inter-country matches a country code and a length and normalizes to E.164. Intra-country uses the site’s country and does the same.

docs.ti: Test emergency like a change, not like a demo
docs.ex: Test emergency like a change, not like a demo. A live emergency test is a carrier and public-safety conversation. The call simulator is the part you can do alone. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: Use the product call simulator for classification and normalization. Use a maintenance window and the carrier’s approved method before any live emergency test.

docs.ti: A forecast is a WFM plan for interactions, not a routing method
docs.ex: A forecast is a WFM plan for interactions, not a routing method. Workforce management is one WEM product. The forecast article names the metrics and the permissions. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The WEM article is the family: recording, quality, speech and text analytics, and workforce management. The forecast article is narrower.

docs.ti: Short-term weeks can schedule. Long-term weeks cannot
docs.ex: Short-term weeks can schedule. Long-term weeks cannot. Six weeks of intervals on one side. Up to two years of days and weeks on the other. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The forecast article describes two views. The short-term view is interval-level data, one week at a time, for up to six weeks depending on the forecast length, and it can generate

docs.ti: Four creation methods, and a 130-week outer limit
docs.ex: Four creation methods, and a 130-week outer limit. Automatic best method, weighted history, imported source days, or a finished short-term file. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The add-a-forecast article lets you pick a start week up to 26 weeks in the past or 104 weeks in the future. The end date cannot pass 130 weeks from the start week.

docs.ti: The editor shows history as read-only lines
docs.ex: The editor shows history as read-only lines. Short-term granularity is 15, 30, or 60 minutes. Long-term granularity is daily or weekly. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: The forecast editor article puts Short-Term Forecast and Long-Term Forecast on two icons. Short-term granularity choices are 15 minutes, 30 minutes, and 60 minutes.

docs.ti: The schedule has to sit inside the short-term weeks
docs.ex: The schedule has to sit inside the short-term weeks. Generation offers a forecast only when those weeks cover the schedule, and only one schedule is generated at a time. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The schedules article lists three generation choices: create a schedule with a forecast, create one without a forecast, and create a blank schedule.

docs.ti: Use the forecast, then go back to the floor
docs.ex: Use the forecast, then go back to the floor. Intraday compares the plan with what happened. Adherence is a different WFM page. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The workforce management overview lists developing forecasts and comparing the intraday forecast with actual values, next to blank schedules, forecast-based schedules, and schedule

docs.ti: What Genesys Cloud CX is
docs.ex: What Genesys Cloud CX is. Genesys Cloud CX is a subscription contact-center platform with four nested packages, not a single feature switch. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: The overview article names four packages. Genesys Cloud CX 1 is the voice package: inbound and outbound voice, secure IVR, callbacks, and voice campaigns.

docs.ti: Core regions and satellite media
docs.ex: Core regions and satellite media. An organization is born in one core AWS region. Satellite regions carry media. They do not host the org. Unconfirmed: Other core regions exist on the same article, including Canada, Ireland, Frankfurt, London, Tokyo, and more. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: When an organization is created, Genesys Cloud deploys it in a core region and sends users to that region’s login URL. US East (N.

docs.ti: SIP, RTP, and what the trunk is doing
docs.ex: SIP, RTP, and what the trunk is doing. SIP sets the call up. RTP moves the audio. They are different protocols, and Genesys trunks speak both. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: RFC 3261 is the Session Initiation Protocol. An INVITE offers a session, responses such as 100, 180, and 200 move the dialog along, and ACK confirms the 200.

docs.ti: What ACD is before you name a queue
docs.ex: What ACD is before you name a queue. ACD picks an agent for a waiting interaction. The queue is the waiting line. Skills, utilization, and On Queue decide who is eligible. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: Genesys Cloud queues are the waiting lines. An agent enters the queues they belong to by choosing On Queue.

docs.ti: Digital conversations beside voice
docs.ex: Digital conversations beside voice. Voice is one media. Architect also has inbound message, email, and chat flows, and queues track those medias separately. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The Architect home page lists inbound message, inbound email, and inbound chat alongside inbound call. In-queue flows exist for calls, email, and messages.

docs.ti: Divisions, before roles get complicated
docs.ex: Divisions, before roles get complicated. A division groups objects inside one organization. It is not a second org, and the Home division cannot be deleted. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: Administrators group configuration objects into divisions and then grant roles against those divisions. A queue lives in one division.

docs.ti: How to read a Genesys page without inventing the rest
docs.ex: How to read a Genesys page without inventing the rest. This lab cites the Resource Center, the Developer Center, Genesys Education, and RFCs. The page wins when they differ.
docs.eg: Implementation facts in this lab were checked against public pages on 14 October 2026.

docs.ti: Prerequisites before the first trunk
docs.ex: Prerequisites before the first trunk. BYOC Cloud needs a public carrier address, an open port plan, and a real location. The org subscription has to include the telephony product you intend to use. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The BYOC Cloud quick start assumes the organization exists and the BYOC Cloud product is on the subscription.

docs.ti: Nothing imports your old routing by magic
docs.ex: Nothing imports your old routing by magic. You rebuild flows, queues, and trunks. You do not flip a converter this lab has not found. Unconfirmed: Lifecycle dates for Engage and PureConnect must be confirmed on Genesys notices. This lesson does not set one. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: Genesys Engage routing strategies and PureConnect handlers do not become Architect flows because a project plan says “migrate”.

docs.ti: Engage and PureConnect become flows and queues
docs.ex: Engage and PureConnect become flows and queues. Strategies, IRDs, and handlers are read as behavior, then redrawn. Unconfirmed: Do not treat WarmTransfer or any third-party blog as Genesys’ lifecycle notice. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: Treat a Genesys Engage routing strategy or IRD as a description of menus, data dips, and targets. Treat PureConnect handlers and queues the same way.

docs.ti: IVR becomes Architect tasks, menus, and audio
docs.ex: IVR becomes Architect tasks, menus, and audio. CVP, UCCX prompts, and Engage voice all become the same kind of flow. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: Create a flow is the article for the voice tasks you will rebuild: play audio, collect input, decisions, transfers, data actions.

docs.ti: UCCE skill groups and precision queues are not Genesys queues
docs.ex: UCCE skill groups and precision queues are not Genesys queues. Membership, skills, and bullseye are three ideas you reassemble. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: Cisco’s UCCE pages describe skill groups and precision queues as that product’s targeting. In Genesys Cloud a queue has members, and skills sit on the agents.

docs.ti: UCCX is a smaller center with the same rebuild rule
docs.ex: UCCX is a smaller center with the same rebuild rule. Scripts, CSQs, and the Finesse desktop do not move as files. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: Cisco’s UCCX series page is the door to that product’s scripts, contact service queues, and agent desktop.

docs.ti: CUCM stays. BYOC is the door, not a replacement cluster.
docs.ex: CUCM stays. BYOC is the door, not a replacement cluster.. A dial plan and a trunk are Genesys number plans and a BYOC trunk. CUCM is still yours. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The migration studio’s CUCM row points at BYOC PBX or BYOC Carrier, and at Dynamic Cloud Voice for new cloud trunks. Genesys does not absorb the CUCM cluster.

docs.ti: Webex is a neighbor, not a page this lab pretends to summarize
docs.ex: Webex is a neighbor, not a page this lab pretends to summarize. Use Cisco’s product pages. Do not cite a Webex help URL this lab did not confirm. Unconfirmed: No specific Webex Contact Center article was confirmed for this lab. Attach your own. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: Webex Contact Center and Webex Calling show up in the same migrations as CUCM. This lab did not confirm a specific Webex help article to deep-link, so it will not invent one.

docs.ti: Cut over one number, then the queue, then the people
docs.ex: Cut over one number, then the queue, then the people. A weekend big-bang is how untested emergency routes meet a full staff. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: Order: a lab number through the new trunk or Edge, the emergency classification tested the way the emergency article allows, one published inbound flow, one published in-queue flow

docs.ti: Place the organization in a core region
docs.ex: Place the organization in a core region. You do not move an org between regions as a setting. You create it in a core region and live with that login host. Unconfirmed: The Voice article also lists planned or limited regions such as Mexico Central and the European Sovereign region. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The regions article is explicit: the organization is deployed in a core region chosen from its location, and users sign in on that region’s URL.

docs.ti: Roles are permission lists paired with divisions
docs.ex: Roles are permission lists paired with divisions. A role without a division grant does not open objects. An OAuth client inherits only a subset of its creator’s pairs. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: Divisions overview is the access model: you grant a role on a division, and the user sees objects in that division. Queues, users, and flows are configuration objects you place.

docs.ti: Named licenses and the concurrent peak
docs.ex: Named licenses and the concurrent peak. Concurrent billing charges the peak of simultaneous users, and it ignores peaks shorter than 30 minutes. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: The concurrent licensing article says Genesys charges the maximum number of simultaneous users in the billing period, after discarding peaks shorter than 30 minutes.

docs.ti: Pick CX 1, CX 2, CX 3, or CX 4 on purpose
docs.ex: Pick CX 1, CX 2, CX 3, or CX 4 on purpose. Match the package to the job. Do not buy CX 1 and then design a WFM project. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: Use the overview as the menu. Voice-only operations fit CX 1. Omnichannel plus quality fits CX 2. Scheduling, forecasting, and the transcription minutes that WEM expects fit CX 3.

docs.ti: People, queues, and the 5,000 member line
docs.ex: People, queues, and the 5,000 member line. Users live in the org. Queue membership is not the same thing as a division, and it has a hard cap. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: Create the person, place them in a division, and grant a role. Membership on a queue is a further step, capped at 5,000 members, and the queue itself sits in one division.

docs.ti: Fair use is a pool, not a mystery invoice
docs.ex: Fair use is a pool, not a mystery invoice. Licenses include monthly allowances. Overage is priced on the policy page. Copying the numbers into a design doc freezes them wrong. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: The fair use policy describes consumption on top of the user license: BYOC Cloud minutes, data storage, basic routing and IVR, API requests, voice transcription, BYO SMS, workitems

docs.ti: A first-week admin checklist
docs.ex: A first-week admin checklist. Week one is region, divisions, roles, packages, one queue, and a published in-queue flow. Telephony can follow. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: Create or confirm the org in the right core region. Create the divisions you will actually administer. Grant roles in pairs. Assign packages that match the scope.

docs.ti: Predictive Engagement watches the site, not the queue math
docs.ex: Predictive Engagement watches the site, not the queue math. It predicts what a visitor is trying to do and offers a message, a chat, content, or a flow. Predictive routing is a different feature on the queue. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: The About Predictive Engagement page calls it a Genesys Cloud AI feature that analyzes how visitors behave on websites, predicts the outcomes they are trying to reach, and personal

docs.ti: Messenger tracks web messaging. The old snippet tracks web chat.
docs.ex: Messenger tracks web messaging. The old snippet tracks web chat.. Genesys tells Genesys Cloud CX customers to use web messaging. Leaving both snippets on the page double-counts the visit. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: The about page says you can use web messaging with Predictive Engagement and encourages web messaging instead of web chat.

docs.ti: A segment matches visitors who meet every condition you listed
docs.ex: A segment matches visitors who meet every condition you listed. At least one condition. More conditions, fewer visitors. Conditions are not shared with the next segment. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: The use case describes a segment as a way to categorize visitors by shared behavior and attributes.

docs.ti: An action map is qualified before it is offered
docs.ex: An action map is qualified before it is offered. Segment, visitor activity, and outcome probability are the trigger kinds. Priority breaks a tie. Web chat is the legacy action. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: Creating an action map starts with a name and an action: web messaging, web chat, a content offer, or an advanced orchestration flow. You then set what triggers it.

docs.ti: Journey Outcomes have a published end date
docs.ex: Journey Outcomes have a published end date. Announced 18 May 2026. Planned effective date 29 June 2026. Outcome scoring is not part of the Customer Outcomes replacement. Unconfirmed: Read on 15 October 2026. The planned effective date on the announcement was 2026-06-29. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: The deprecation announcement lists the announced date as 2026-05-18 and the planned effective date as 2026-06-29.

docs.ti: An Architect flow can be the action, and it can also be the thing you must edit
docs.ex: An Architect flow can be the action, and it can also be the thing you must edit. Advanced orchestration is an action type. Flows that still call getJourneyOutcome need a path that does not depend on it. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: The about page lists Architect workflows and Architect flow actions as the way to integrate Predictive Engagement with other systems, including a listed topic for Salesforce lead c

docs.ti: Prove the map with Live Now and the performance reports
docs.ex: Prove the map with Live Now and the performance reports. Visitor activity and action-map performance are the Predictive Engagement reports. Outcome columns age out with the deprecation. Unconfirmed: The use case names action types web chat, content offers, and Architect flow.
docs.eg: The about page points supervisors at live visitor tracking, visitor activity, and action-map performance, and at journey columns on Genesys Cloud performance views.

docs.ti: Quality management evaluates the conversation
docs.ex: Quality management evaluates the conversation. QM records and scores interactions, and it can coach. It is not the schedule. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: The quality article describes evaluation forms, policies, calibration, coaching, disputes, and the ability to evaluate in-progress or recorded interactions.

docs.ti: Forms have questions and weights
docs.ex: Forms have questions and weights. The form is the rubric. Weights decide which questions move the score. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: The QM article points at evaluation form weights and at creating forms. A form that weights greeting at 80 percent and resolution at 5 percent will congratulate short polite calls

docs.ti: Recording policies choose calls and retention
docs.ex: Recording policies choose calls and retention. A policy decides which ACD calls are recorded and how long they are kept. A secure flow is a hole in a segment, not a substitute for the policy. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: About recording says you use policies to choose ACD calls and retention, and that a user can also record their own calls.

docs.ti: Coaching and disputes close the loop
docs.ex: Coaching and disputes close the loop. A score that the agent cannot see and cannot dispute is not a quality program. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The QM article lists coaching appointments, evaluation disputes, and managing those disputes. It also lists monitoring and coaching in-progress interactions.

docs.ti: AI scoring needs STA, QM, and tokens
docs.ex: AI scoring needs STA, QM, and tokens. The FAQ is blunt: AI scoring requires Speech and Text Analytics, Quality Management, and AI Experience Tokens. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: The STA FAQ says AI scoring needs the interaction transcribed, and that Virtual Supervisor AI scoring needs STA, QM, and AI Experience Tokens.

docs.ti: Retention, export, and the reason you recorded
docs.ex: Retention, export, and the reason you recorded. Export and AWS recording paths exist so a recording can leave the platform under a policy, not as a side copy. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The QM article mentions AWS recording export among the tools around evaluations. About recording points at related articles for listening and for S3-style recording paths.

docs.ti: Quality evaluates the interaction. Speech analytics reads it
docs.ex: Quality evaluates the interaction. Speech analytics reads it. The quality article says speech and text analytics runs on 100 percent of interactions. That is a claim to re-open, not a sample size you invent. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: The about-quality-management article says quality management lets managers record and evaluate agents and interactions, and coach them.

docs.ti: A question is human, AI scored, or assisted by topics
docs.ex: A question is human, AI scored, or assisted by topics. The form article names three automation choices. Evaluation focus is Full Interaction or Evaluated Agent. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The create-and-publish article, as the automated-scoring article points at it, gives each question one of three choices: No Automation, AI Scoring, or Evaluation Assistance.

docs.ti: AI scoring waits for history, and a low week hides the answer
docs.ex: AI scoring waits for history, and a low week hides the answer. A rolling window of 25 submissions. Below 75 percent, the answer is hidden. The transcript needs 300 characters. Unconfirmed: This lesson states the 300-character criterion because that is the threshold written in the notes section opened in 2026-10. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The automated-scoring article says AI scoring runs only when the conversation meets at least one of its criteria, and the criterion written in the notes this lab could read is a tr

docs.ti: Phrases make a topic. Topics make a program
docs.ex: Phrases make a topic. Topics make a program. A program is mapped to queues or flows, and it can turn sentiment and empathy on or off. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: The programs, topics, and phrases article defines the dictionary. A phrase is a string of words for one way to say something, typed one by one or uploaded, and words outside the st

docs.ti: Programs have counts, and the organization switch wins
docs.ex: Programs have counts, and the organization switch wins. One hundred programs. Five hundred topics per dialect. Twenty scoring rules. Sentiment off at the org turns it off everywhere. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: The work-with-a-program article’s create section states these limits: 100 programs in the organization, 20 tags on a program and on a topic, 500 queues and 500 flows on one program

docs.ti: Agent scoring picks which agent receives the evaluation
docs.ex: Agent scoring picks which agent receives the evaluation. Each, first, or last matched agent. The article also says the last participant is the evaluated agent. Unconfirmed: The program article lists Each, First, and Last Matched Agent, and also says the last agent to participate is assigned as the evaluated agen Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The program article’s agent-scoring section lists three generation choices: Each Matched Agent creates an evaluation for every matched agent, First Matched Agent only the first, an

docs.ti: Create the queue in a division
docs.ex: Create the queue in a division. The queue is a named waiting line in one division, with at most 5,000 members. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: Menu path in the article is User Management, then Queues. You set a unique name without special characters, an optional peer id for an external platform, the division, and an optio

docs.ti: Skills and proficiency are on the agent
docs.ex: Skills and proficiency are on the agent. The queue asks for skills. The agent profile holds them. Evaluation decides whether proficiency matters. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: ACD skills are tags with a proficiency. All-skills matching ignores the number and demands the tag.

docs.ti: After call work and the system wrap-up codes
docs.ex: After call work and the system wrap-up codes. ACW is optional, discretionary, or time-boxed. The platform has its own codes when agents do not finish. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: Optional ACW lets the agent skip wrap-up. Mandatory discretionary lets them end ACW themselves. Mandatory time-boxed caps the duration.

docs.ti: Wrap-up codes live in divisions too
docs.ex: Wrap-up codes live in divisions too. The codes an agent sees are the codes their role can see, and Genesys wants them in the queue’s division. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The queue article says you add wrap-up codes that your role can see, and it recommends codes assigned to the same division as the queue so reports make sense.

docs.ti: Service level is a percentage and a target in seconds
docs.ex: Service level is a percentage and a target in seconds. Each media has a service level percentage and a target duration. That pair is what conditional routing and WFM both mean by “the goal.” Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: The queue article tells you to set a service level percentage and a service level target in seconds per channel.

docs.ti: Callbacks are interactions with their own rules
docs.ex: Callbacks are interactions with their own rules. A callback is queued work. It still needs a wrap-up code, and it counts as its own utilization slot. Unconfirmed: Scheduled callbacks are called out separately from inbound callbacks on the preferred-agent page. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: CX 1 includes callbacks. The utilization default is one callback, and preview calls are treated as callbacks.

docs.ti: Membership, On Queue, and the copy trap
docs.ex: Membership, On Queue, and the copy trap. A copied queue can duplicate a bullseye you did not mean to clone. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: Membership is the list of agents who may receive the queue’s work, up to 5,000. On Queue is the status that actually enters them.

docs.ti: ACD is the match, and skills are one way to make it
docs.ex: ACD is the match, and skills are one way to make it. Wikipedia describes an ACD as a distributor. Genesys Cloud puts that job on the queue’s routing method. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The Wikipedia article describes an automatic call distributor as a system that answers and distributes incoming calls, and it describes skills-based routing as routing by an operat

docs.ti: Three evaluation methods, and a seven-day lookback
docs.ex: Three evaluation methods, and a seven-day lookback. All skills matching, best available skills, and disregard skills do different jobs. Proficiency covers ACD skills and language skills together. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: All skills matching selects the agent who has every required skill and the longest time since the last interaction. It does not use the skill rating.

docs.ti: Bullseye widens the pool in two documented ways
docs.ex: Bullseye widens the pool in two documented ways. One way adds skill-expression groups. The other removes skills. The ring count is not the same sentence on every page. Unconfirmed: Opened in 2026-10: the settings article says define up to five rings and, later, up to six. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: The bullseye overview describes expansion as concentric rings. Option 1 adds agents from groups on the next ring, and it tells you to use skill expression groups with the same skil

docs.ti: A skill expression filter replaces the queue’s skill list
docs.ex: A skill expression filter replaces the queue’s skill list. It works for standard and predictive routing when evaluation is All skills matching. Other methods ignore it. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The evaluation article describes an optional ACD skill expression filter. You define a combination of skills and proficiencies in Architect, or supply it through the API, and Genes

docs.ti: Direct routing still uses a queue
docs.ex: Direct routing still uses a queue. The customer reaches a dedicated person. Wrap-up still exists, because the interaction is ACD. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The direct routing overview says you route voice, SMS, and email to dedicated personnel, and the customer does not wait for the next available agent.

docs.ti: Preferred scores are 0 to 100, and the list has a size
docs.ex: Preferred scores are 0 to 100, and the list has a size. Architect’s agent-score collection supports 20 pairs unless Customer Care raises it. More than 20 fails a call flow. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The advanced routing overview says a preferred-agent score is the agent’s priority, from 0 to 100, and the highest score is the most preferred.

docs.ti: STA reads the conversation after the channel has it
docs.ex: STA reads the conversation after the channel has it. Speech and text analytics covers voice and digital interactions. It is not a second ACD. Unconfirmed: Confirm dialect coverage and any per-minute price on the current STA pages. This lesson does not list them. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: The overview and the about page describe transcription and analysis of voice interactions and of digital interactions such as email, message, and chat.

docs.ti: Sentiment is a label on the text, not a mood you can argue with
docs.ex: Sentiment is a label on the text, not a mood you can argue with. Sentiment scores the customer’s language. Use it as a filter, then listen. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The STA pages describe sentiment so you can find interactions that went badly or well without listening to all of them.

docs.ti: Topics, programs, and phrases are the dictionary
docs.ex: Topics, programs, and phrases are the dictionary. A program groups topics. A topic is phrases you expect to hear or read. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The STA overview describes topics and programs so you can find whether a phrase occurred: a competitor, a cancel request, a required disclosure. Phrases are the dictionary.

docs.ti: Agent empathy is a detected behavior, still a form question
docs.ex: Agent empathy is a detected behavior, still a form question. Empathy detection points at calls. Calibration still decides what empathy means for your company. Unconfirmed: Confirm the current trigger filters on the STA pages before you automate anything from empathy. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: The STA material describes agent empathy as something you can detect and later filter on, including for process-automation style triggers when the current article lists that filter

docs.ti: Content search is how you test the dictionary
docs.ex: Content search is how you test the dictionary. Search the transcript before you trust a topic count. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The STA pages describe content search so you can find interactions by what was said or written. Use it when a topic count looks wrong. Search the phrase.

docs.ti: Full analysis and a faster transcript are different clocks
docs.ex: Full analysis and a faster transcript are different clocks. Some views wait until the interaction is complete. A lower-latency transcript path is a different API. Unconfirmed: AudioHook and other streaming connectors must be confirmed on the current article. This lesson does not rank vendors. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The STA FAQ and overview distinguish analysis that completes after the interaction from lower-latency transcript delivery through the Notifications API.

docs.ti: WEM is a set of products, and WFM is one of them
docs.ex: WEM is a set of products, and WFM is one of them. Recording, screen recording, quality, performance, speech and text analytics, and workforce management are the WEM list. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: The WEM article names those capabilities together. WFM is the planning half: business units, management units, service goal templates, planning groups, activity codes, schedules, a

docs.ti: Business units and management units
docs.ex: Business units and management units. A business unit is the planning container. A management unit is the group of agents you actually schedule. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The WEM article tells you to configure business units and management units before schedules. Agents in a management unit share the planning rules you are about to write.

docs.ti: Service goal templates are the planning target
docs.ex: Service goal templates are the planning target. The queue’s service level and the WFM template should describe the same promise. Last checked 2026-10. Unconfirmed if the vendor page has moved.
docs.eg: The WEM article lists service goal templates among the objects you configure. The queue article is where the live percentage and target seconds are set, per media.

docs.ti: Schedules are the plan agents work
docs.ex: Schedules are the plan agents work. A schedule is built from the management unit, the goals, and activity codes. It is not a routing method. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The WEM article includes schedules and activity codes in the WFM list. Activity codes mark what an agent is supposed to be doing: on queue, break, meeting, training.

docs.ti: Intraday and adherence compare the plan to the floor
docs.ex: Intraday and adherence compare the plan to the floor. Adherence is the gap between the activity you scheduled and the status the agent is actually in. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The WEM article lists real-time and historical adherence and intraday monitoring. Intraday is how you change today when the morning forecast was wrong.

docs.ti: Time off is a schedule change with a rule
docs.ex: Time off is a schedule change with a rule. Time-off requests are part of WFM. An approved request that nobody reflects on the schedule is a rumor. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The WEM article lists time-off requests beside schedules and adherence. A request that is approved in mail and never entered in WFM will show the agent as absent against a schedule

docs.ti: The workforce certification is a named exam
docs.ex: The workforce certification is a named exam. The catalog lists a Workforce Management specialist certification and a preparation course. It does not list a code this lab is willing to invent. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: On the Genesys Education cloud exam page, Workforce Management Certification is a specialist exam. The recommended preparation is the course titled WEM – Workforce Management.

docs.ti: A forecast has a short view and a long view
docs.ex: A forecast has a short view and a long view. Short-term data can build a schedule. The long-term view is for seasonality and does not generate one. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: The workforce management overview lists developing forecasts, comparing intraday forecast to actual values, and three schedule styles: blank, forecast-based, and without a forecast

docs.ti: Generate one schedule from a forecast that covers it
docs.ex: Generate one schedule from a forecast that covers it. The schedule period has to sit inside the short-term forecast, and a business unit generates one schedule at a time. Last checked 2026-10.
docs.eg: Schedules can be created with a forecast, without a forecast, or blank. With a forecast, the engine uses the forecast plus work-plan constraints.

docs.ti: Downloads
